vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: pixmind-image
Version: 1.0.0

The skill facilitates image generation via the Pixmind API (aimix.pro) but relies on executing external Node.js scripts (image-generate.js, task-status.js) located outside the skill's immediate directory. This pattern of shell execution using user-provided prompts introduces a potential command injection risk, and the reliance on external paths is a risky capability that warrants caution, although no explicit malicious intent or data exfiltration logic is present in the provided files.

llm.summary: The skill’s instructions mostly match an image-generation purpose, but there are multiple unexplained mismatches (API host doesn't match the claimed vendor, model names look inconsistent, and the docs reference local helper scripts that are not included), so proceed with caution.

dimensions.detail: The skill is advertised as 'Pixmind' but the documented API endpoint is https://aihub-admin.aimix.pro/... which does not obviously match Pixmind branding or a known Pixmind public API. The listed model names include Google-branded models (imagen, gemini) which is unusual to bundle under a single third-party endpoint and is not explained. There is also no homepage or source URL and the owner ID is opaque. These branding and provenance mismatches could be benign (third-party aggregator or proxy) but are not justified by the SKILL.md.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs the agent to use helper scripts at {baseDir}/../../scripts/image-generate.js and task-status.js, but the skill bundle contains no code files or scripts. The instructions therefore encourage the agent to run local Node scripts that are not part of the skill and whose presence and content are unknown. Aside from that, the API usage (POST endpoint, X-API-Key header, JSON body, polling) is in-scope for image generation.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec and no code files — this is instruction-only, so nothing will be written to disk by an installer. That minimizes installation-time risk.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill only requests a single env var PIXMIND_API_KEY, which is appropriate for an API-based image generation skill. However, because the SKILL.md sends requests to an unexpected domain (aihub-admin.aimix.pro) and the skill has no homepage/source, it's unclear where that API key will be sent or who controls the receiving service. That lack of provenance increases risk of credential misuse or misrouting.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request always: true and does not ask to modify other skills or system settings. It is user-invocable and allowed to run autonomously (normal defaults).
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
This skill looks like it intends to call an image-generation API, but several red flags mean you should verify before installing or providing a real API key:

- Confirm the vendor and endpoint: ask the publisher where PIXMIND_API_KEY will be sent and whether ai hub (aihub-admin.aimix.pro) is an official Pixmind endpoint. If you can't verify the endpoint from an official Pixmind source, treat it as untrusted.
- Missing helper scripts: SKILL.md references local Node scripts that are not included. Ask the publisher to provide those scripts or update the instructions so the agent doesn't try to run arbitrary local code.
- Limit the key's scope: if you decide to test, create a limited/test API key with minimal quota and monitor usage and logs closely.
- Prefer a skill with clear provenance: a homepage, source repo, or official vendor documentation that matches the API host and model names.

If you cannot confirm the endpoint and scripts, do not provide your real PIXMIND_API_KEY and consider rejecting the skill.
